## Research Experience

::: entry
Sep. 2026 – Present

**Independent project: reinforcement-learning models of the Iowa Gambling Task**

I taught myself R and Stan, implemented eight reinforcement-learning models of the Iowa Gambling Task from their published equations, and compared them on held-out choices from open data. A curvature extension of ORL that I introduced (ORL + α) predicted best, and on a new sample of 70 people it met all five predictions I wrote in advance. In a preregistered replication (N = 440), all ten predictions were met: a stacked mix of the models outpredicted the best single model (z = 12.5). I then showed that two published models share a mathematically identical term and combined them into a new model, NOVA. The mix weights NOVA most heavily, and that result replicated against predictions committed in advance. Latest results: [alejandrohinojosa.com/research](https://alejandrohinojosa.com/research.html) and [github.com/AlejandroHinojosa2005/IGT-Modeling](https://github.com/AlejandroHinojosa2005/IGT-Modeling).
:::

::: entry
Aug. 2026 – Present

**Nonprofit project** · Together For Good, Waco, TX

For a Behavioral Medicine course taught by Dr. Annie T. Ginty, I worked on a four-person team supporting Together For Good, a nonprofit that prevents child abuse and neglect by connecting families in crisis with volunteer caregivers who temporarily care for their children. I built and managed the team's outreach database, researching and organizing contact information for 100 local businesses and tracking every response. I reached out to all 100 businesses, generating 14 responses, including 2 donation commitments and 12 businesses interested in future partnership. I also helped research and compile 70 grant opportunities into a shared spreadsheet for the organization's future funding efforts.
:::

::: entry
July 2026 – Present

**Research Assistant** · Social-Personality Research Laboratory, Baylor University, Waco, TX

I worked with Dr. Wade Rowatt on a study using Wave 1 of the Global Flourishing Study (N = 202,898) across 22 countries. I looked at whether a country's dominant K–12 pedagogical tradition predicts two things schooling is often said to shape: adults' sense of personal mastery and their approval of their nation's government. I built a nine-category classification of countries from the comparative-education literature because none existed, preregistered three hypotheses on OSF, and ran every analysis in R, including a wild cluster bootstrap I implemented from the methods literature when no package supported our version of R. [Preregistration](https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/J9T4F)
:::

::: entry
Jan. 2026

**Research Assistant** · Joshua Cabrera, MD, College Station, TX

I worked with Dr. Joshua Cabrera, MD, a psychiatrist in College Station. We looked at his deceased patient population with schizophrenia. The goal was to find links between medications taken by patients and exacerbation of certain conditions such as hypertension and diabetes which may lead to premature death. This research was used internally to gauge whether taking a certain medication is worth the risks given certain biomarkers.
:::

**Hospice Volunteer** · Alamo Hospice, Waco, TX

I build rapport and meet with hospice patients for an hour biweekly. I listen to the patients, allowing them to share their concerns, regrets, and/or areas of thankfulness. I encourage the patients to share their life story or share what is on their mind.

Sep. 2024 – Present

:::
